sentence: This project uses proteomics and genomics to look for molecular targets for treatments that prevent cardiovascular complications related to atrial cardiopathy.
This project tries to find out how a protein that T cells need helps them destroy tumors during cancer immunotherapy.
This project studies resilience to aging at the molecular, cellular, organ, and systemic levels to identify therapeutic targets.
This project develops non-toxic precision medicines for gliomas, a form of brain cancer in children and young adults.
This project measures arsenic and uranium in drinking water and studies how they relate to cancers, aiming to reduce exposure in communities.
This project builds deep learning tools that use clinical MRI data to guide surgery for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy.
This project applies automated analysis to routine medical imaging to find aortic aneurysms missed by current screening and learn how they develop over time.
This project studies how a protein complex controls the nuclear export of modified mRNAs in castration-resistant prostate cancer.
This project studies the behavioral and neural mechanisms of social motivation in rats with a gene mutation used as a model for autism spectrum disorder.
This project tests whether specific types of inhibitory neurons are more effective at suppressing epileptic activity without disrupting information encoding.
This project uses deep sequencing to study the genetics of pigtail macaques in a research colony used to study HIV infection.
This project designs and improves genome and epigenome editing tools to study how hematopoiesis is connected to cardiovascular diseases.
This project studies the structure of alpha-synuclein fibrils to better understand disease mechanisms in Lewy Body Dementia.
This project builds statistical software that helps scientists study the effects of genetic variation and find sets of related genes.
This project uses AI and machine learning approaches to help researchers analyze neurophysiology data from open datasets.
This project offers next generation sequencing and single cell genomics support to investigators who study cancer.
This project studies how synapses differ between neuronal subtypes and how they develop, to understand how neural circuits form.
This project studies which genes, when improperly regulated, cause heart defects, using mouse and human models including models of Down Syndrome.
This project measures environmental chemicals present before diagnosis to find patterns that predict future risk of mature B-cell neoplasms.
This project uses complex video stimuli and functional neuroimaging to find brain regions that predict autism spectrum disorder groups and traits.
